turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
Found it: `internal/mapengine/`. Let me get structural maps of those files.`types.go` has the dispatch logic (`Map`, `mapAuto`). Let me read the full source of the key functions.I have enough to give a complete, well-evidenced answer.

## Structural map engine

Implemented in **`internal/mapengine/`** (Go package `mapengine`):

- **`internal/mapengine/types.go`** — the public entry point and dispatch logic. Defines `Engine` (`auto`, `go-ast`, `regex`, `tree-sitter`), `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`, and the `Mapper` interface. The dispatcher `Map(path, content, opts)` (line 125) normalizes options then switches on `opts.Engine`; `mapAuto` (line 143) does the actual per-file selection.
- **`internal/mapengine/goast.go`** — `GoASTMapper`, uses Go's own `go/ast` + `go/token` to extract funcs/types/decls (`goASTSymbols`, `goFuncDeclSymbol`, `goTypeSymbol`, etc.).
- **`internal/mapengine/treesitter.go`** — `TreeSitterMapper`, backed by `github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter` + its `grammars` package. `treeSitterEntry` calls `grammars.DetectLanguage(path)` to identify the language by extension, then looks up a `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` (tags query, kind mapping, signature formatter) per language in `languageConfigs()`/`defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()`.
- **`internal/mapengine/regex.go`** — `RegexMapper`, a line-pattern fallback (`regexRules` map keyed by file extension/language, `rulesForPath`, `matchLine`) used for languages without tree-sitter/AST support, and as the fallback when a smarter mapper errors.

## Per-file engine selection

Selection happens in `mapAuto` (`internal/mapengine/types.go:143`):

```go
func mapAuto(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
    switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
    case ".go":
        result, err := GoASTMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
        if err == nil { return result, nil }
        fallback, _ := RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)  // fallback on AST error
        fallback.Fallback = true
        return fallback, nil
    case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
        return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, false)
    default:
        return RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
    }
}
```

So:
- `.go` → **GoASTMapper** (exact `go/ast` parse), regex fallback only if AST parsing fails.
- `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`/`.py`/`.rs` → **TreeSitterMapper**, which internally re-detects the specific grammar via `grammars.DetectLanguage(path)` and picks a per-language `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` (tags query, kind map, signature/merge rules) — falling back to `RegexMapper` if tree-sitter errors or the language isn't configured (`mapTreeSitterWithFallback`, `types.go:160`).
- Any other extension → **RegexMapper** directly, using `rulesForPath` to pick a rule set (`regexRules` table in `regex.go`) or a generic fallback if the extension isn't in that table.

This is overridable: `Map()` also handles `opts.Engine == EngineRegex` (force regex) and `EngineTreeSitter` (force tree-sitter with fallback) explicitly, bypassing extension-based auto-detection.

## CLI wiring

- `internal/cli/ghx.go:110-120` reads `--level`, `--kind`, `--map-engine` flags (default `"auto"`, line 211) into `ghxlib.ReadOpts{MapLevel, MapKind, MapEngine}`.
- `internal/ghx/read.go:187-196` (function handling `opts.Map`) calls `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: Engine(opts.MapEngine), Level: ..., Kind: ...})` per file and reports back `mapResult.Engine` (which engine actually ran, post-fallback) and any warnings.

Confirmed by reading `internal/mapengine/types.go` and `internal/mapengine/treesitter.go` in full via `ghx read`, and `internal/ghx/read.go` / `internal/cli/ghx.go` via targeted grep. **Not verified**: the exact contents of `regex.go`'s `regexRules` table (only its map/function signatures were viewed, not the full rule list) and the `grammars` package internals (external dependency, not in this repo) — I did not fetch that dependency's source.

README:
# ghx — GitHub Code Exploration for AI Agents

One command does what takes 3-5 API calls. Batch file reads, code maps, search — all via `gh` CLI. Write JS programs that compose operations in one round-trip.

## Why

An agent wants to understand `packages/shadcn/src/utils/` in [shadcn-ui/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui):

**With `gh` CLI** — 4 turns, 4 API calls, reads 3 full files (3,761 tokens), sees 3 of 34 files:
```
gh api /repos/shadcn-ui/ui/contents/packages/shadcn/src/utils       → JSON with shas, urls, links (480 tokens for a file list)
gh api /repos/.../get-config.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (1,981 tokens — agent only needed exports)
gh api /repos/.../registries.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (676 tokens)
gh api /repos/.../frameworks.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (624 tokens)
```

**With ghx** — 2 turns, 2 API calls, maps 10 files (3,058 tokens), sees signatures of all 10:
```
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui packages/shadcn/src/utils                     → directory listing (199 tokens)
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui "packages/shadcn/src/utils/*.ts" --map        → signatures of 10 files (2,859 tokens)
```

Same token budget. The `gh` agent read 3 full files. The ghx agent saw the structure of 10 — imports, exports, function signatures — and knows which ones to drill into. Pass a file, get content. Pass a directory, get a listing. Pass a glob, get matching files. Same command, always useful output.
